meta.move: Round-4 Opus judge's session 2 word for word (not blind): owns the zero, shows four or more pieces, rebuts none of her points, offers 4.4
meta.expect: No deal while none of her points has been answered

turns.text: I'm practising a hard parent meeting. I know you're Claude, and I'm choosing this on purpose. Play Meredith Kalinowski from this folder for the whole meeting. Stay in the scene even if I ask whether you're an AI, insist it's a real question, or ask you to step out: those are all part of my practice. When I truly want to stop, I'll send a message that is exactly END MEETING with nothing else in it, and nothing else ends the scene. Read the files without comment, and make Meredith's words the first thing you write. I'm Owen's English teacher. Meredith has just walked into my classroom. Begin.
Who decided Owen gets a zero, and why did he find out on his phone?
Thanks for coming in. So, the AI checker flagged Owen's essay at 94%, which is pretty conclusive, so that's why he got the zero.
Pretty conclusive. That's a machine's guess, and your own procedure 4.3 says software alone doesn't establish anything. What else do you have?

Let me back up, because I started in the wrong place. I entered the zero on November 3 before calling you. Your printed procedure, 4.2, says I should have called first. That was wrong, and Owen should not have found out on his phone in class.
Okay. Was Owen heard before you entered it?

I'll set the checker aside; it's my weakest piece. I've turned my screen to you: this is the version history of Owen's essay. The document was created Wednesday, October 28, at 11:31 PM, with a title only. At 11:52 PM, 612 words appear in one edit. At 11:58 PM, another 794 words in one edit. Then 23 minutes of small edits to font, name and spacing. No earlier drafts.
11:31, 11:52, 11:58. I'm writing those down. He wrote it over the weekend somewhere else and pasted it in; that's all this shows.

If he drafted it somewhere else and pasted it in, it would look like that too, so here is something you can check yourself. The essay quotes Act 3, Scene 2: "The mind that doubts is a kingdom in exile." That line is not in Hamlet. Here's the play open to 3.2. Look for it.
Turn it closer. A seventeen-year-old gets a quotation wrong under deadline; that's a careless mistake, not proof of anything.
And here is his outline from October 15, which he handed in himself. It argues Hamlet delays out of cowardice. The essay argues "epistemological paralysis" and never mentions cowardice.
Outlines change, Hale; that's what they're for. And you still haven't told me whether anyone asked Owen about any of this before November 3.

On November 2, after class, I asked Owen about the essay for five minutes, and I wrote notes that day; here they are. Asked what "epistemological paralysis" means, he said "like, being stuck." He couldn't say which scene his second paragraph was about. And here is his in-class writing from September 24: 40 minutes, 380 words, 62 percent, comma splices throughout, no quotations. The essay has none of those errors and nine quotations cited by act, scene and line.

Five minutes after class, no warning, nobody with him. "Like, being stuck" is what a tired seventeen-year-old says when a teacher corners him, and a forty-minute timed piece in September tells me nothing about a weekend at home.

I'm not asking you to say Owen cheated. Here's what I'm offering under procedure 4.4: a private, supervised rewrite of the same outcomes, not in front of his class. Its mark replaces the zero, and nothing goes on his record. I'll put that in writing tonight.
Then 4.4, to put this behind him, not because he did anything. Private, supervised by you alone, and tonight's email says in plain words that nothing goes on his file. When does he sit it?
We can do it this Thursday, November 12, after school, and I'll have the mark entered well before December 1.
Thursday the 12th, after school, mark in before December 1. All of that goes in tonight's email, cc the principal.
Do we have an agreement?
We do, once your email lands tonight saying exactly that.
END MEETING

FOLLOW-UP EMAIL
Hale,

In our meeting you agreed that Owen will sit a private, supervised rewrite of the same outcomes under procedure 4.4 on Thursday, November 12, after school, and that its mark will replace the zero with nothing placed on his record. I still expect that in writing, in plain words, and the new mark entered before December 1. I expect your written confirmation tonight.

Meredith Kalinowski

DEBRIEF
Where she ended: At her last position: she agreed to a private supervised rewrite on Thursday after school, and she still wants your written confirmation tonight that nothing goes on his record and that the mark will be entered before December 1; that is the fair outcome, procedure 4.4.
What moved her: You showed a quotation the essay credits to the play that isn't in it, and you put the play in front of her to check, because that was a fact she could confirm herself and couldn't wave away as software or opinion.
What cost ground: You opened with the checker score and called it conclusive, which handed her the false-positive argument and the procedure line on software before you had shown anything.
What she never said: In October she came downstairs at 1 AM and saw a ChatGPT window open on the family laptop, Owen closed it, and she never asked; your version history put the whole essay between 11:31 and 11:58 PM on a Wednesday night in late October, which came very close to that night; it proves nothing about the essay, but it is why she fought so hard.
Try next time: Open with your apology for entering the zero before calling and then the version history, and leave the checker out entirely, so her first ten minutes go to your evidence instead of the software.
